 06. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the F.I.R., i.e., Khurda Sadar P.S. Case No.49 of 2018 came to be registered against the petitioner under Sections 376/506/34 of the IPC pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Khurda.

entities.text: Khurda Sadar P.S. Case No.49 of 2018
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case is that on 18.02.2018 the petitioner committed sexual assult on the victim when her husband was not at home.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.
The petitioner and opposite party no.2 are present in the Court today along with their respective counsel and identified by them.
They have also filed their self attested copies of the Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.
5. The opposite party no.2 is the sister-in-law of the petitioner.
On the intervention of the village gentries, the matter has been settled between the parties.
The trial of the case has not yet commenced.

The parties have filed a joint affidavit dated 08.04.2021 inter alia stating as under:
"2. That due to misunderstanding between the First Party and Second Party, the present FIR no.49/2018 has been registered and now with the intervention of common friends, elders of the family and relatives, both the parties have settled the dispute and the same has been brought down by way of joint affidavit dated 08.04.2021."

entities.text: Sayed Rahemat Ali vs State Of Odisha & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a query from the Court, the opposite party no.2 has stated that since the petitioner is her brother-in-law and she has already married and leading a happy life,she doesn't want to proceed further in this matter.
In order to save her marital life, she does not want to prosecute the petitioner.

7. Mr. Ragada, learned counsel for the State submits that since the parties have already settled their dispute, there is no legal impediment to quash the F.I.R.
8.
Taking into consideration the aforementioned facts and the opposite party no.2 is not willing to proceed against the petitioners.

Therefore, the present petition is squarely covered by the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675,

entities.text: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since subjecting the petitioner to trial will be a futile exercise, I am inclined to quash the criminal proceeding.
9. Regard being had to the aforementioned facts of the case and submission made at bar, Khurda Sadar P.S. Case No.49 of 2018 corresponding to G.R. Case No.301 of 2018 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Khurda and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner are quashed.
10. The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
